text: 🇲🇽✊ "We are a humanist government with a feminist heart." — Mara Lezama, Governor of Quintana Roo, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Social policy as the axis, a gender lens, and attention to the roots of inequality — not just its symptoms. The framing for a mañanera held, for the first time, from Tulum, Quintana Roo.

🇲🇽🎨 The Jaguar Park in Tulum will be free — and Mexicans pay a fraction to see their own heritage. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Free entry to Parque del Jaguar. The archaeological zone: 80 pesos for Mexicans, 265 for foreigners. Electric transport, 20 pesos. The dividing wall comes down, replaced by a Maya-designed arch. The heritage belongs to the people, not to speculation.

🇲🇽🔍 Targets wanted by the US and Europe — captured on Mexican soil, under Mexican law. — Omar García Harfuch, Security Secretary, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Priority targets requested by the United States and European countries were detained in Quintana Roo by Mexican forces. Oct 2024–June 2026: 3,794 arrests, 6,688 kg of drugs and 762 firearms seized. Cooperation, not subordination.

🇲🇽🔍 Quintana Roo: homicides down 85%. From nearly two killings a day in September 2024 to 0.3 in June 2026 — the lowest month in 12 years. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Tulum: two straight months with zero homicides, and July still clean at report time. High-impact crime down 15% year over year. The result of the governor's work and the Security Cabinet's coordination.

🇲🇽✊ "Honesty, love for the people and the homeland — of course they deliver results." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 They said security couldn't improve without an iron fist or deals with the powerful. Quintana Roo just posted an 85% drop in homicides. Fighting corruption from the top down is the first security policy of the Fourth Transformation.

🇲🇽✊ "The beaches belong to the people, and they're free." Mexico's federal government opened 10 public accesses to Tulum's beaches — reversing years of hotels privatizing the coastline. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 The sea and the shore are national property: open and free for residents, national tourists, and foreigners alike. Part of Plan Tulum.

🔥🇲🇽 A former PAN governor just got caught running fuel smuggling. Ernesto Ruffo Appel — ex-governor of Baja California — was detained for organized crime and "huachicol fiscal," the fuel-contraband racket that has drained billions from the nation. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 "In reality, it's fuel smuggling." A year-long investigation by the FGR; eight arrest warrants executed. If he has proof of innocence, she said, it goes through the Mexican justice system.

🇲🇽🌎 US WANTS TARIFFS AND QUOTAS TO CAP MEXICAN EXPORTS — BECAUSE MEXICO IS SELLING TOO MUCH

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told the Aspen forum he has "a mandate from the president" to shrink the trade deficit with Mexico "whether through tariffs, quotas or any other mechanism." That deficit hit a record 197 billion dollars in 2025, up 17% in a year — Mexico now sells Washington so much the empire wants rules to make its own market buy less. Greer still calls the Mexican negotiators "quite pragmatic," with a third round of T-MEC talks set for Mexico City. (via El Financiero)

🇲🇽📚 CDMX'S FREE COMMUNITY SCHOOLS PARTNER WITH A PUBLIC UNIVERSITY

PILARES — the network of free education, culture and sports centers running since 2019 across Mexico City's 16 boroughs — signed an agreement with UAM Cuajimalpa to professionalize the facilitators who staff them. The aim, officials said, is that "teacher professionalization will transform the social environment of benefited neighborhoods." Public university training public educators for working-class barrios, tuition-free.

🇲🇽💧 20 BILLION PESOS TO CLEAN MEXICO'S THREE MOST POISONED RIVERS

Sheinbaum's government is putting 20 billion pesos this sexenio into sanitizing the Atoyac, Lerma-Santiago and Tula — the country's most contaminated rivers — through 93 coordinated projects reaching 25 million people across 10 states. Crews have already mapped 3,202 industrial and domestic discharges and 479 clandestine dumps; stage-one work is 90% complete on the Lerma-Santiago. "It's about protecting life and guaranteeing a better future," Sheinbaum said.
